articles.title: A Quality Initiative for Posterior Spinal Fusion in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS): Liposomal Bupivacaine With Dexamethasone Use Results in Substantial Reduction in Inpatient Opioid Use.
articles.authors: Stuedemann A, Huston M, Saddler N, Anderson J, Benvenuti M, Sherman AK, et al.
articles.population: Adolescents aged 10 to 18 years with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing posterior spinal fusion
articles.sample_size: 159 patients (88 intrathecal morphine, 36 intravenous methadone, 35 liposomal bupivacaine with dexamethasone)
articles.outcomes: Inpatient opioid consumption (morphine milligram equivalents per kilogram), length of hospital stay, and pain scores
articles.take_home: Using liposomal bupivacaine injected into the muscle with intravenous dexamethasone, and removing patient-controlled pain pumps, substantially reduced the amount of opioids needed after spinal fusion surgery whilst keeping pain control effective and shortening hospital stays. Eighty percent of patients receiving this approach went home on day two after surgery compared with 27-42 percent in the other groups.

articles.title: Outcomes of Distal Radius Autograft in Adolescent Scaphoid Nonunion Repair.
articles.authors: Rupp GE, Rea PM, Curran PF, Bomar JD, Edmonds EW, Wallace CD
articles.outcomes: Union achieved in all wrists at mean 3.3 months post-surgery; improved wrist alignment on X-rays; 94% returned to activities at mean 9.6 months; no intraoperative complications
articles.take_home: Surgery to repair scaphoid nonunion using bone graft from the forearm was successful in all adolescent patients, though return to normal activities took about 10 months. Improved alignment of the wrist bones was seen on X-rays after surgery.

articles.title: Serial Casting and Hinged Elbow Bracing in the Treatment of Fixed Flexion Deformity of the Elbow Following Obstetric Brachial Plexus Palsy.
articles.authors: Simpson AI, Kwok IH, Liechti R, Sinisi M, Panagiotidou A, Fox M
articles.population: Children with obstetric brachial plexus palsy and fixed flexion deformity of the elbow
articles.outcomes: Change in active elbow flexion deformity measured before and after treatment; complications; premature termination; recurrence requiring repeat treatment
articles.take_home: Serial casting and hinged elbow bracing improved elbow straightening by an average of 25 degrees, with most children needing only one course of treatment and few complications. The treatment worked well even when repeated in children whose deformity returned.

articles.title: Brace non-adherence and relapse after Ponseti treatment for idiopathic clubfoot: a focused updated scoping review.
articles.authors: Arvati S, Zokou H, Luc F
articles.population: Children with idiopathic clubfoot treated with Ponseti method
articles.sample_size: 25 studies in focused update (19 empirical studies and 6 contextual/grey-literature items)
articles.outcomes: Brace adherence, relapse rates, factors affecting adherence including brace tolerance, access, cost, transport, caregiver understanding, and care continuity
articles.take_home: Not wearing the brace as prescribed after clubfoot treatment is linked to the foot returning to its original position, and this is often caused by practical problems like transport difficulties, cost, missed appointments, and poor understanding rather than simple non-compliance. Better organised care and support with these practical issues could help children stick to their brace treatment.

articles.title: Intraosseous 'Synthetic Teretization' in the absence of ligamentum teres: surgical technique and early results.
articles.authors: Sarassa C, Aristizabal S, Garcia JJ, Quintero D, Mejia R, Herrera Torres AM
articles.population: Paediatric patients with high-grade developmental dysplasia of the hip (IHDI grade III-IV) and absent ligamentum teres
articles.sample_size: 9 hips in 8 female patients, median age 24 months
articles.outcomes: Hip stability, range of motion, McKay score, pain, complications, radiographic assessment including IHDI and Severin classification, acetabular index, and avascular necrosis
articles.take_home: All nine hips remained stable and painless with no redislocation or avascular necrosis at median 23-month follow-up. Synthetic teretization using a button-suture-button construct is a feasible option to stabilise the hip when the ligamentum teres is missing.

articles.title: Bone healing and functional outcomes of utilizing contralateral free vascularized fibular graft following en bloc resection of adamantinoma and osteofibrous dysplasia-like adamantinoma.
articles.authors: Petitpas C, Girardin C, Peltier E, Guillaume JM, Jouve JL, Pesenti S, et al.
articles.population: Children and young people with tibial adamantinoma or osteofibrous dysplasia-like adamantinoma treated with en bloc resection and reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Bone healing and graft remodeling, functional scores (Musculoskeletal Tumor Society score), complications, and cancer recurrence
articles.take_home: Using a bone graft from the other leg to rebuild the tibia after removing an adamantinoma tumour led to good bone healing (averaging 11.5 months) and functional results, with most patients remaining cancer-free after more than 9 years. However, complications like graft fractures and infections did occur, so careful planning and long-term monitoring are important.

articles.title: Children in all policies: lessons from a global collaboration to promote the health and wellbeing of children and future generations.
articles.authors: Dalglish SL, Sakyi KS, Prost A, Amin S, Sardesi A, Mudaly A, et al.
articles.population: Children and policy makers across diverse countries
articles.outcomes: Eight lessons for effective policy making: involving children creatively, building coalitions, seizing political opportunities, harmonising global data, creating national platforms, using media, strategic framing, and joint learning
articles.take_home: Children's voices and needs are often left out of public policies, which harms their health and wellbeing. A global collaboration has found that including children in decision-making through creative methods, building partnerships across different sectors, and changing how people think about children's issues can lead to better policies for healthier futures.

articles.title: Fracture morphology and multidirectional instability in failed closed reduction of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures.
articles.population: Children aged 2-12 years with severe upper arm bone fractures near the elbow
articles.sample_size: 318 children (192 successful closed reduction, 126 requiring open reduction)
articles.outcomes: Success of closed reduction based on fracture type and stability; flexion-type fractures had 80% open reduction rate; Gartland type IV instability strongly associated with need for open surgery
articles.take_home: Certain fracture patterns, particularly flexion-type breaks and unstable fractures, are much more likely to need open surgery rather than closed reduction. Recognising these patterns helps surgeons prepare and plan the best approach for treatment.

articles.title: Rock-paper-scissors-OK game for neurological examination in pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: A prospective randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Aydin T, Inci F, Kilic M, Yigit N, Kahve Y, Ceyhan E
articles.population: Children aged 4-10 years undergoing surgery for supracondylar humerus fractures
articles.outcomes: Nerve examination time before and after surgery, child and parent satisfaction with communication and information sharing, frequency of agitation, crying and non-compliance during examination
articles.take_home: Children who learned nerve examination using a smartphone game were assessed faster after surgery and were less upset during the process, compared to those taught using traditional methods. Parents and children also felt better informed when the game method was used.

articles.title: Five-year MRI follow-up of growth-related complications after ACL reconstruction in children and adolescents.
articles.authors: de Pesters C, Laval A, Staali L, Flumian C, Faruch M, Accadbled F
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with five-year MRI follow-up
articles.population: Skeletally immature children and adolescents undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Physeal-diaphyseal angles, Harris growth arrest line deviation, bone bridge formation, physeal closure, and clinical growth disturbances on MRI
articles.take_home: Transphyseal ACL reconstruction in growing children causes minimal growth-related changes on imaging that are clinically insignificant. Small bone bridges formed in 19% of patients but resolved on their own, and no permanent growth problems were identified.

articles.title: Effectiveness of a Structured Training Program in Pediatric Distal Radial Fracture Reduction for Orthopaedic Advanced Practice Providers.
articles.authors: Nair A, Teti B, Fay C, Bowen MA, Olson AM, Sarkar S, et al.
articles.population: Children undergoing distal radial fracture reduction in emergency department settings
articles.outcomes: Post-reduction angulation, percent contact on radiographs, loss of reduction rates, need for subsequent surgery
articles.take_home: Advanced practice providers who received structured training achieved better initial fracture reductions and lower rates of loss of reduction and surgery compared with junior resident doctors. The structured training programme enabled APPs to deliver effective fracture care independently.

articles.title: Watchful waiting versus methylprednisolone or polidocanol injections as treatment of simple bone cysts.
articles.authors: van Geloven TPG, Soffers AMJ, Fiocco M, van der Heijden L, van Kouswijk HW, de Witte PB, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with competing risk analysis
articles.outcomes: Cumulative incidence of healing, cumulative incidence of failure, prognostic factors for healing and failure
articles.take_home: Immediate injection treatment for simple bone cysts leads to better healing than watchful waiting or delayed treatment. Polidocanol injections work better than methylprednisolone injections for both healing and preventing failure.

articles.title: Weaning in INfant hip DYsplasia (WINDY) study: weaning of brace treatment versus immediate cessation for developmental dysplasia of the hip : study protocol for a randomized multicentre feasibility study.
articles.authors: Craven J, Kirk R, Griffin XL, Conroy E, Carpenter EC, Llewellyn-Stanton L, et al.
articles.population: Infants with developmental dysplasia of the hip treated with Pavlik harness who have achieved ultrasound normalization
articles.outcomes: Feasibility outcomes: recruitment, proportion randomized, parental engagement and compliance. Secondary outcomes: acceptability of gradual weaning versus immediate cessation, measurement properties of EMBRACE questionnaire, feasibility of using Smart4NIPE data for trial outcomes.
articles.take_home: This feasibility study will test whether it is practical to run a large trial comparing two different ways of stopping Pavlik harness treatment for baby hip dysplasia: gradually reducing wear over four weeks versus stopping immediately. The study will help determine if a full trial is possible and whether parents find questionnaires acceptable for measuring their experience.

articles.title: Do Prophylactic Antibiotics Decrease Risk of Infection in Closed Percutaneous Pinning of Pediatric Hand Fractures?
articles.authors: Ho CA, Chaudhry S, Gottschalk HP, Bauer A, Freese K, Onubogu C, et al.
articles.population: Children undergoing closed reduction percutaneous pinning for closed finger and hand fractures
articles.outcomes: Superficial infection rates: 0.2% with antibiotics versus 2.01% without antibiotics
articles.take_home: Children who received prophylactic antibiotics before hand fracture pinning surgery had significantly lower superficial infection rates than those who did not. Overall infection rates were low and similar to previous studies.

articles.title: Spinal Fusion Concurrent With Construct Removal Is the Preferred End Point of the Shilla Growth Guidance Procedure.
articles.authors: ElNemer W, Elsabbagh Z, Cha MJ, Andras L, Akbarnia BA, Bumpass DB, et al.
articles.population: Children with early-onset scoliosis treated with Shilla growth guidance procedure who reached skeletal maturity or had implant removal
articles.sample_size: 74 patients (mean age at implantation 6.8 years, 65% female)
articles.outcomes: Major coronal deformity progression, instrumentation-related complications, deep wound infection rates, need for subsequent spinal fusion surgery
articles.take_home: Children who had their Shilla implant removed and spinal fusion done immediately had fewer infections (6%) than those who had fusion later (22%), and fewer cases of severe curve worsening. Keeping the Shilla implant in place after growth stops still carries risks of complications, so immediate fusion at the time of implant removal may be the better approach.

articles.title: Comparing Caregivers' Perspectives on the Health-related Quality of Life of Children With Cerebral Palsy.
articles.authors: Wang A, Bone JN, Juricic M, Miller SD, Wu J, Mulpuri K, et al.
articles.population: Children with severe cerebral palsy (GMFCS levels IV and V) and their caregivers
articles.sample_size: 50 caregiver pairs (100 caregivers) with children averaging 9.5 years old
articles.outcomes: Differences in CPCHILD questionnaire scores between pairs of caregivers for the same child
articles.take_home: Different caregivers of the same child with severe cerebral palsy give different scores on quality of life questionnaires, with an average difference of 7.5 points between caregiver pairs. This suggests that using different caregivers to complete the questionnaire over time may affect how treatment outcomes are measured and compared.

articles.title: A Novel Technique for Intraoperative Navigation in Occipitocervical Fusion: A Preliminary Report.
articles.authors: Cohen L, Guilbault R, Pradhan P, See AP, Hogue G
articles.outcomes: Intraoperative complications, navigation accuracy, occipital fixation complications
articles.take_home: A new way of using navigation during spine surgery in children had no complications related to navigation or bone fixation in three cases. This approach may save time and make the surgery safer by improving alignment of the spine fusion.
